source_title: TJ Reid: Kilkenny's seven-time All-Ireland winner retires from inter-county hurling - BBC
source_excerpt:
Kilkenny's seven-time All-Ireland winner TJ Reid has announced his retirement from inter-county hurling.
Reid joined Kilkenny's senior panel in 2007 and went on to win 14 Leinster senior titles, five National Hurling League medals and seven All-Star awards.
The 38-year-old was named hurler of the year in 2015 and also became the all-time leading scorer in senior hurling championship history with 43 goals and 672 points.
"TJ Reid has given extraordinary service to Kilkenny hurling over almost twenty years. His achievements speak for themselves, but it is the manner in which he represented Kilkenny, his commitment to the jersey, and the standards he set throughout his career that will leave a lasting impression," Kilkenny GAA Chairman PJ Kenny said in a statement.
"He has been a wonderful ambassador for Kilkenny GAA and a firm favourite with our supporters, who have enjoyed so many memorable moments thanks to his exceptional talent.
"On behalf of Kilkenny GAA, I want to sincerely thank TJ for everything he has given to our county."
The Shamrocks Ballyhale clubman also won six All-Ireland Senior Club titles and 13 Kilkenny Senior Hurling Championship medals.
"After 20 seasons in black and amber, I have decided to bring my Kilkenny senior hurling career to an end," Reid posted on social media.
"Walking away from something that has been such a huge part of my life is not easy, but I leave with immense pride and no regrets.
"When I first wore the Kilkenny jersey in 2007, I never imagined I would still be representing my county two decades later. It has been the greatest privilege of my life."
